prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1357; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision at an intersection where the insured vehicle was turning left and was struck by an oncoming vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the first notice of loss. They show damage to the front quarter of the insured vehicle that is largely consistent with the impact described in the initial report.

Entry 3: Police report and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the parties and the photographs.

Entry 4: Checked the vehicle's prior claim history and inspection records. No earlier damage to this vehicle has been found in any file.

Entry 5: Verified that the policy was in force on the date of loss and that no lapse or late endorsement is indicated. Nothing in the file points to damage predating coverage.

Entry 6: The driver of the insured vehicle resides with the named policyholder and is listed as a household member, so coverage applies under the policy's household provisions.

Entry 7: Medical records received show a neck strain as the primary diagnosis. The injury type and the force involved in the crash appear to align well, and treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this presentation.

Entry 8: Records also show treatment to the same area of the neck within the last two years. That prior condition appears to be adding to the current complaints, and the apportionment question has been noted for review.

Entry 9: The claimant has given the same account of events in every recorded conversation, and the details have not shifted between contacts. File remains open pending the medical review and counsel's demand package.
